claims: The Fab Five refers to the 1991 University of Michigan men's basketball recruiting class consisting of Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King, and Ray Jackson.
The Fab Five were the first all-freshman starting lineup to reach an NCAA Championship game.
The Fab Five reached the NCAA finals in 1992 and 1993.
Fab Five members include Chris Webber (#4), Jalen Rose (#5), Juwan Howard (#25), Jimmy King (#24), and Ray Jackson (#21).
The Fab Five were known for wearing baggy shorts and black socks.
The Fab Five reached the 1992 NCAA title game and lost to Duke.
The Fab Five reached the 1993 NCAA title game and lost to North Carolina.
The Fab Five were involved in the University of Michigan basketball scandal regarding improper payments from booster Ed Martin.
The University of Michigan basketball scandal led to the school forfeiting their records.
The Fab Five members reunited for a special alternative broadcast during the 2026 NCAA Final Four on truTV and HBO Max.
Four Fab Five members went on to play in the NBA.
Juwan Howard won two NBA championships.
